To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed efficient techniques for feature-based image/video access and manipulation, including feature-based image/video retrieval, feature-based image/video editing and manipulation, and feature-based image/video summarization.

we have developed a new framework for feature-based indexing and retrieval of images and videos, based on the concept of “feature vector.” We have also developed a number of techniques to efficiently manipulate feature-based image/video archives.
we propose a novel approach to image and video indexing and retrieval that is based on a new feature extraction and indexing technique.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) How to efficiently and effectively represent visual contents in a way that is both domain-independent and user-friendly; and (2) How to efficiently search for visual contents based on the representation.
the problem of how to efficiently and effectively index, search, and retrieve images and videos in a VIS system.
developing techniques to index and retrieve images and videos in a way that is both automatic and content-based.

there is a great need for a method to automatically generate the index for image and video databases.
the text-based search methods are not effective enough in VIS.
a VIS system should be equipped with a feature-based image/video access and manipulation system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the goal is to develop efficient techniques for feature-based image/video access, retrieval, and manipulation.
we are developing techniques to enable efficient and effective access to visual information.
we are trying to develop a system that can provide an efficient and effective way for users to retrieve images/videos from large archives based on visual contents, i.e., image/video features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can effectively use the content of images/videos for image/video retrieval, and the techniques we have developed can be applied to a wide variety of VIS applications.
the visual content of images can be used as a powerful tool for indexing and searching.
a visual information system can be designed to be domain independent and can be easily adapted to any application domain.
